key_insight: In patients with normal PET perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve, and zero coronary calcium, ascending aortic calcium still identified a subgroup with higher residual cardiovascular risk.
clinical_relevance: A routinely available, fully automated measure from attenuation-correction CT may help refine risk stratification when standard PET readouts appear reassuring.
method: Multicenter REFINE-PET registry cohort of 21,923 patients; analysis focused on 3,580 triple-normal patients.
Ascending aortic calcification (AAC) was automatically segmented from non-contrast CT using deep learning and Agatston scoring.
Outcomes were assessed with adjusted Cox models for cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, heart failure admission, and all-cause mortality.
evidence_signal: AAC showed good agreement with blinded readers (ICC 0.87-0.90) and was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24) with only modest discrimination gains beyond clinical and PET measures.
watch_item: The added predictive gain was modest, so AAC may be better viewed as a risk-refinement marker than a standalone decision tool until prospective implementation is validated.
paper_title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
